findings.issue: resolveRoleSlugsByIds (grants-dao.ts) is written and documented as a BULK resolver (dedup + ANY($2::uuid[]) tenant-scoped read), but the wiring in publishProcessByKey invokes it once PER userTask-ref inside mapUserTaskRoleToCandidateGroups's internal loop (one query per distinct roleId, each with a 1-element array) rather than collecting all extractUserTaskRoleRefs(...) roleIds up front and resolving them in a single call. Functionally correct (per-process diagrams have few userTasks, and each call is its own tenant-scoped read-tx) — this is a latency/roundtrip nit, not a correctness bug.
findings.suggestion: Optional follow-up: have mapUserTaskRoleToCandidateGroups accept a batch-resolving port (roleIds: string[]) => Promise<Map<string,string>>, or have the process-defs.ts wrapper pre-resolve extractUserTaskRoleRefs(...).map(r => r.roleId) once and hand mapUserTaskRoleToCandidateGroups an in-memory lookup. Not blocking for this fix.

findings.issue: Routing proof stops at 'deployed XML string contains flowable:candidateGroups="<slug>"' plus a separate unit/db proof that resolveRoleSlugsByIds resolves id->slug correctly. Nothing in this diff exercises getHoldersForRole/inbox.ts consuming that exact candidateGroups value end-to-end to prove it lands in a real holder's pool. This matches the established test-depth convention for the sibling publish-transform mappers (lane-role-mapper T-0457, agent-task-external-mapper T-0635) — executor-resolver.test.ts / inbox tests cover the slug-matching contract generically, not per fixing-task — so this is consistent with prior practice, not a regression in rigor.
